This appeal has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated
23.02.2021 passed by the Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, Principal Mact, Bengaluru
(for short `Tribunal'), in Mvc No.6187/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.  For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.
3. This matter is slated for admission, with the consent of both the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

4. The brief facts of the case of both the parties before the Tribunal were that :
On 08.09.2019 at 9.30 a.m, the deceased met with an accident at Neeladri Road in front of Concord apartment due to rash and negligent driving of two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-43-W-0603 (for short 'offending vehicle).
NC: 2025:KHC:44606 HC-KAR
As a result, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and while undergoing treatment succumbed to injuries.
5. It is further contention of the claimants that the deceased was aged 48 years and earning Rs.20,000/- by working as a security guard.
He was contributing his earnings to the family.
Claimants are the wife, minor daughters and mother of the deceased.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.60,00,000/-.
6. Respondent No.1 was the insurer and respondent No.2 was the owner of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.2 remained exparte before the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal and filed its written statement, denying its liability to pay the compensation.
With these reasons, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
7. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues, for its determination.
NC: 2025:KHC:44606 HC-KAR 8.
The claimants to prove their case examined one witness as PW-1 and marked 13 documents as per Exs.P-1 to P-13.
The respondent No.1 has not led any oral or documentary evidence.

9. The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence on record, awarded following amount of compensation:
 Particulars

Amount in Rs.
 Loss of dependency 16,08,828

Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of consortium 40,000  Funeral and ritual expenses 15,000  Loss of parental consortium to 80,000 Smt G Nagendramma vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Insurance Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173571850/
3  Loss of filial consortium to petitioner 40,000  No.4  Total 17,98,828  Rounded off 17,99,000/-
Being dissatisfied with the award passed by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Heard the arguments of both side.
The fact of the accident and death of Gorla Gangadhar in the said accident are not in dispute.

The Tribunal assessed the age of the deceased as 48 years and took notional income as Rs.11,000/- per month, applied multiplier as '13' and deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses and in all awarded compensation of Rs.17,99,000/-
12.
The claimants contend that deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
They were unable to substantiate the same.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken income of the deceased as Rs.11,000/- per month, which appears to be on the lower side comparing notional income chart prepared by KSLSA.
Following the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income is taken as Rs.14,000/- per month.
There is no dispute in respect of age, addition of 25% of income towards future prospects, multiplier applicable and deductions.
13. On the basis of the aforesaid factors, the amount of compensation is recalculated under the head `loss of dependency'.

It is the further submission of learned counsel for the appellant that, as per the law laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi1 and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
-vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram,2 the amount of compensation awarded under the conventional heads are also on the lower side.

sentences.text: Therefore, prayed to enhance the same.

15. As per the law laid down in Pranay Sathi's case (supra) and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
case (supra), the Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation under the head loss of consortium to each claimant.
In view of the above said reasons, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires re-assessment and enhancement.

16. Accordingly, the following compensation is awarded:

19. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii) The judgment and award dated  23.02.2021 passed in  MVC.No.6187/2019 by the Chief  NC: 2025:KHC:44606  HC-KAR Judge, Court of small causes, Member Prl.MACT, Bengaluru stands modified;
iii) The claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,39,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced amount, from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The respondent No.1 shall deposit the amount within a period of six weeks from the date of award.
v) The apportionment, deposit and release etc., are as per the award passed by the Tribunal.
